mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment rate above 5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises above 5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate coupled with high CPI suggests inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS is low and CPI is high but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, high federal funds rates lead to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS is high in a tightening cycle but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing non-farm payroll employment signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: PAYEMS increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Housing starts are high but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Balanced growth in industrial production and GDP indicates stable economic conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO and GDPC1 growth is balanced but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, low unemployment rates signal economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE is low in late-cycle but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.
